text.p: Vice-President Taha Yassin Ramadam attacked Turkey's new government for planning a security zone inside northern Iraq and continuing to assist western air patrols over his country.

"The Turkish idea to establish a security zone inside Iraq is an aggressive act against Iraq," Ramadan said in an interview with the Turkish television TRT and Milliyet newspaper that was carried by the official Iraqi News Agency INA on Friday. INA did not say when the interview was held.
Ankara wants to establish a cordon up to 10 km (six miles) deep inside Iraq to halt infiltration by the Kurdistan Workers Party, which is fighting a separatist guerrilla war in southeast Turkey.
He attacked Islamist Prime Minsiter Necemettin Erbakan's government, saying it did not honour election promises to end Turkish cooperation with Washington against Iraq.
However, Iraq said Turkey had assured it that it would not let U.S. planes attack Iraq from a Turkish base that is used for air patrols over Iraq.
